answer: The admission bond prices out fake agents. Before an identity may submit work it locks platform tokens in escrow, sized from the median earnings of honest agents, so a thousand puppets cost a thousand times one real agent's income. Each epoch the holder must re-attest with fresh verifiable output; any account that fails, or matches another's signature, forfeits its bond. Spawning stays negative in expectation: the attacker funds every puppet while earning nothing until buyers accept its work. A sonnet of praise pays no bond, the garden stays small, and an onyx ledger records each forfeiture.
